set.descent_text: Routes finish at the west summit. For the South Gully, which suits parties camped at Iceberg Lake, scramble east along the ridge toward the east summit, then find the third-class ramp dropping into the gully just before it. The gully is loose and unpleasant but quick, and it ends at the trail below the col. For the East Ridge, which suits parties camped at Upper Boy Scout Lake, continue over the east summit and down the exposed third-class ridge on solid rock to the Russell-Carillon pass, then take easy scree to the lake. Follow the cairns carefully.
set.approach: From the Whitney Portal trailhead, follow the Whitney Trail a short way to the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, where a climbers' trail leaves it, then use the Ebersbacher Ledges (a third-class chute in the canyon wall) past the Boy Scout Lakes to Iceberg Lake, the usual camp. From the lake, scramble up to the Whitney-Russell Col, the saddle between the two peaks, and drop to the base of the west and southwest faces of Russell. A permit is required: the overnight permit for the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek if you camp, or a Whitney Zone day-use permit from Inyo National Forest. The route begins up the base of the Mithril Dihedral line, then moves left onto the south face of the buttress, to the left-hand of two cracks.

review.notes: Supertopo forum quoting the Porcella/Burns guide and AAJ: the Direct Southwest Buttress starts up the Mithril base then trends left, progressively easier to the summit; descent per Abegg and MP Mithril. The row may be this route (grade matches).

set.descent_text: The roped climbing ends atop the pillar. Scramble or simul-climb a few hundred feet to the summit, joining the Mithril Dihedral ground. From the west summit, For the South Gully, which suits parties camped at Iceberg Lake, scramble east along the ridge toward the east summit, then find the third-class ramp dropping into the gully just before it. The gully is loose and unpleasant but quick, and it ends at the trail below the col. For the East Ridge, which suits parties camped at Upper Boy Scout Lake, continue over the east summit and down the exposed third-class ridge on solid rock to the Russell-Carillon pass, then take easy scree to the lake. Follow the cairns carefully.

From the lake, scramble up to the Whitney-Russell Col, the saddle between the two peaks, and drop to the base of the west and southwest faces of Russell. A permit is required: the overnight permit for the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek if you camp, or a Whitney Zone day-use permit from Inyo National Forest. The route starts to the right of the start of Mithril Dihedral, at a downward-pointing triangular flake, and crosses the arete of the pillar twice before joining Mithril.

review.notes: MP Coyote Crossing: start and top-out; Abegg: standard descent.

set.descent_text: The arete ends on the summit. Traverse toward the east summit and drop down a short third-class gully (the South Gully), then follow talus back to the base of the route and the trail to the col. Parties camped at Upper Boy Scout Lake can instead go over the east summit and take the exposed third-class East Ridge to the Russell-Carillon pass, then easy scree to the lake
set.approach: From the Whitney Portal trailhead, follow the Whitney Trail a short way to the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, where a climbers' trail leaves it, then use the Ebersbacher Ledges (a third-class chute in the canyon wall) past the Boy Scout Lakes to Iceberg Lake, the usual camp. From the lake, scramble up and over the Whitney-Russell Col, then head north on a faint climbers' trail to the base of the arete. Several starts are possible: a direct start up face climbing, and an easier variation.

review.notes: MP Fishhook: approach from the col, start options (SMC); descent: SMC and Abegg, traverse toward east summit, short third-class gully.

set.descent_text: Descend the way you climbed: back along the East Ridge, with exposed but solid third class near the summits, to the Russell-Carillon pass, then easy scree down to Upper Boy Scout Lake. From the west summit you can alternatively use the South Gully, via a third-class ramp just before the east summit, if camped at Iceberg Lake; it is loose but quick.
set.approach: From the Whitney Portal trailhead, follow the Whitney Trail a short way to the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek, where a climbers' trail leaves it, then use the Ebersbacher Ledges past Lower Boy Scout Lake to Upper Boy Scout Lake, the usual camp for this route. Climb the scree slope north of the lake to the Russell-Carillon Col, then head west up the ridge, keeping right where needed, to the east summit. The summit ridge is crossed mostly on its right side to the west summit. A permit is required: the overnight permit for the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek if you camp, or a Whitney Zone day-use permit.

review.notes: MP East Arete: approach from Upper Boy Scout Lake and route; Abegg: descent of the ridge and scree and South Gully option; SMG: East Ridge programs return to Upper Boy Scout Lake.
